title: Sweet Tomato-Onion Pasta Base Cubes
equip: 1 stainless steel pasta pot/stockpot, Philips hand blender, 60ml-cell silicone tray(s) with lid

items.n: canned whole peeled tomatoes (3 x 400 g cans)
baking soda, only if the base tastes sharp

steps.x: Heat the oil on medium. Add the onions and 1 tsp salt. Cook for 10 min, stirring, until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the carrot and garlic. Cook for 3 min, stirring.
Add the tomato paste. Cook for 3 min until it turns brick red.

Add the canned tomatoes with their juice and the remaining salt. Crush the tomatoes with the spoon. Simmer on medium-low with the lid ajar for 35 min, stirring every 5 min, until thick and the oil separates at the edges. This slow cook-down is what removes the sourness.
Take the pot off the heat and blend smooth with the hand blender. If it is still sharp, stir in 1/8 tsp baking soda off the heat (it will fizz), then taste again.
Cool for 30 min with the lid off. Spoon into the 60 ml cells and level the tops.

parts.x: Cool for 30 min with the lid off.
Spoon into the 60 ml cells and level the tops.

steps.x: Freeze uncovered for 3 h until solid. Pop out, bag flat, press out the air and label with name and date.

notes: Use 6 cubes (360 ml) per 400 g dry pasta (4 portions), loosened with pasta water.
For pasta e fagioli, start with 4 cubes (240 ml) in place of the onion-and-tomato stage of your recipe, and adjust to taste.
For a creamy finish without opening cream, stir 1 tbsp butter into the sauce at the end. Butter is safer than milk, which can curdle in acidic sauce.
No herbs or chilli in the base, so you can add oregano, basil or chilli per dish. Plate the child's portion first when adding chilli.
Freezer life: 3 months. Thawed cubes keep 2 days in the fridge. Don't refreeze.
source: None (original; inspired by LifeByMikeG's 5 Flavor Cubes doc)
